doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Time and Love and later records
title: Making the 'Time and Love' album for Creed Taylor
summary: The 1972 album, pitching Creed, and Don Sebesky's orchestrations for a 70-piece orchestra.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: It saved our lives, you know, it saved us. But you know one thing we did leave out, I just remembered that the year before this all happened in 1972 is when we made that album “Time and Love,” which is the album we did for Creed Taylor, and that was such a wonderful time. We were going out to Fire Island in the summer. We were renting a house with our friend Bradley Cunningham, and we’d spent three months out there. And we hadn’t been doing anything because we were doing the commercials. So at one point we said gee we’ve got to record something. We should get back in the studio and do something. And I don’t remember how it came about — oh yeah we were going in and pitch it to Creed. We were going to go in and try and talk him into it.

We’d done maybe four albums for him on Verve and so forth, and we were going to go into the city and just like talk it up — Creed we want to do another album, and like let’s see what we can do, and so we walked in and we started talking, talking, talking, and he says, “that sounds like a good idea, let’s do it.”
He didn’t give us any opposition. We’d just started.
And we’ve still got all this energy — let me tell you about — hey but I—

He was for it right away. And then he got Don Sebesky on it, and of course Don Sebesky contributed such a tremendous amount, because he came up with a lot of the ideas and did all these big charts orchestrating, and of course there were a couple of Roy’s things in there too but he orchestrated everything for a 70 piece orchestra. And it was just, I mean it was thrilling to do it.
You had the cream of the — the best.
The best players of New York.
